title: Separated scheme self-relations of affine charts of finite-inertia DM stacks
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Stacks in groupoids, Deligne--Mumford stacks, representability by algebraic spaces and $2$-fibre products use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-trf-algebraic-space]. Properties of representable maps are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts. For a groupoid in schemes, use the laws of [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]; for algebraic spaces use the same laws on all test-scheme points. Write $[V/R]$ for the fppf stackification of the groupoid of $V(T)$-objects and $R(T)$-arrows [def-pc-fppf-site, lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description]. Let $\mathcal X/S$ be Deligne--Mumford. Its inertia has objects $(x,\alpha)$ with $x\in\mathcal X(T)$ and $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(x)$, arrows given by conjugation, and projection $(x,\alpha)\mapsto x$. Suppose this projection is finite: every scheme base change is represented by a finite scheme morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let $V$ be an affine $S$-scheme and $a:V\to\mathcal X$ a representable etale morphism, not necessarily surjective [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Then $R=V\times_{\mathcal X}V$ is represented by a scheme, and the source and target projections $s,t:R\to V$ are separated and etale, hence flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, pqf-def-quasifinite]. Separated here means closed-immersion diagonal on scheme tests [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The isomorphism triples $(v,w,\alpha:a(v)\xrightarrow{\sim}a(w))$ give its scheme groupoid structure. The stabilizer scheme $G=R\times_{V\times_S V,\Delta_V}V$ is finite over $V$; for every point $v\in V$, $G_v$ represents the automorphisms of the object $a(v)$ over its residue field. The image of $|V|\to|\mathcal X|$ is the point space of an open substack $\mathcal W\subseteq\mathcal X$, and the canonical functor $[V/R]\to\mathcal X$ identifies $[V/R]$ with $\mathcal W$. In particular $[V/R]$ is Deligne--Mumford and this functor is a representable open immersion, hence etale. Here $|\mathcal X|$ means field-valued objects modulo isomorphism after common field extension, with topology detected by a scheme atlas. An open substack is a strictly full substack whose scheme base changes are open subschemes; affine means isomorphic to the spectrum of a commutative ring. A stabilizer fibre is the scheme fibre over $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-fibre-product].

proof.text: The DM stack $\mathcal X$ has diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a surjective etale scheme atlas; etale representable maps are smooth by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], so [lem-sfb-etale-smooth-atlas-fppf-descent] makes $\mathcal X$ an fppf stack, hence an algebraic stack. Apply [lem-sfb-self-relation-quotient-embedding] to $a:V\to\mathcal X$. It gives the algebraic space $R$, its groupoid operations on isomorphism triples, and the canonical fully faithful functor $i:[V/R]\to\mathcal X$. Both projections are base changes of $a$, hence etale by [lem-sfb-dm-etale-atlas-calculus]. Here $V$ is a scheme, thus a DM stack via its identity atlas; no surjectivity of $a$ is used.

The absolute structure map $V\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated], so its diagonal is a closed immersion. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] that diagonal is proper. Thus $V$ is absolutely separated in the stack sense. Apply [lem-sfb-stack-separated-source-separated-inertia-target] to $a$, with source $V$ and target $\mathcal X$: the source hypothesis was just verified and finite inertia is assumed. It follows that $\Delta_a$ is proper. The criterion [lem-sfb-representable-stack-diagonal-criterion] applies because $a$ is representable and converts this into closed-immersion scheme tests of $\Delta_a$.

source.place: Tag 050M (lemma-compose-after-separated), part (3), with Tag 0CL0 (lemma-diagonal-diagonal), part (1), and Tag 04YS (lemma-representable-separated-diagonal-closed); scheme inputs Tags 01KN, 01KV, 01W5.

proof.text: For either projection $r:R\to V$, [lem-sfb-groupoid-diagonal-two-pullback-identities](1) identifies its diagonal with the base change of $\Delta_a$. Every scheme test of that diagonal is consequently a scheme test of $\Delta_a$ and is a closed immersion by step 2. Thus $s,t$ are separated algebraic-space maps. Apply [lem-a1-separated-etale-space-scheme] to $s:R\to V$, whose separatedness and etaleness are now proved: $R$ is a scheme and $s$ is etale. The other projection remains etale on its scheme charts, including the identity chart of $R$, so is etale as a scheme map. Etaleness includes flatness and local finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Finally [lem-a1-etale-space-locally-quasi-finite] applied to each projection, and the identity chart of $R$, gives scheme local quasi-finiteness.

source.place: Tag 0DU3 (lemma-etale-local-quasi-DM), first paragraph; spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 03XU and 03XX.

proof.text: On a test scheme $T\to V$, a section of $G=R\times_{V\times_SV,\Delta_V}V$ is precisely an arrow $(v,v,\alpha)$, namely an automorphism $\alpha$ of $a(v)$. Likewise $V\times_{\mathcal X}I_{\mathcal X}$ has triples $(v,(x,\beta),\theta:a(v)\simeq x)$; conjugation sends this to $(v,\theta^{-1}\beta\theta)$, with inverse $(v,\alpha)\mapsto(v,(a(v),\alpha),1)$. Arrows between such triples are uniquely the comparisons required by this formula. These inverse equivalences commute with pullback, identifying $G\to V$ with the scheme base change of inertia. It is finite by the hypothesis itself. Base changing this same description by $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)\to V$ shows that $G_v$ represents automorphisms of the residue-field object $a(v)$, on all schemes over $\kappa(v)$.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], $a$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. Therefore [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology-flat-lfp-open] makes $|a|$ open. Its image $O$ is open, and [lem-sfb-stack-topology-open-substacks] supplies the strictly full open substack $\mathcal W$ with point space $O$. The map $a$ factors through $\mathcal W$: its pullback open in $V$ corresponds to the full subset $|V|$, so is all of $V$. The factored map is representable etale by base change, using [lem-sfb-dm-etale-atlas-calculus]. It is surjective in the field-extension sense: every field object of $\mathcal W$ has point in $O$, hence becomes isomorphic to an image from $V$ over a common field extension. The definition [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] now gives $\mathcal W$ a surjective etale scheme atlas $V$; its diagonal is representable since it is a full substack of $\mathcal X$. Thus $\mathcal W$ is DM. In particular it is algebraic: etale maps are smooth by the chartwise calculus, and [lem-sfb-etale-smooth-atlas-fppf-descent] makes $\mathcal W$ an fppf stack.

Since $\mathcal W\subseteq\mathcal X$ is strictly full, the self-relation $V\times_{\mathcal W}V$ has exactly the same isomorphism triples and operations as $R=V\times_{\mathcal X}V$. The representable surjective etale map $V\to\mathcal W$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, so [lem-sfb-fppf-groupoid-stack-presentations](2) gives the canonical equivalence $[V/R]\simeq\mathcal W$, compatible with the map from $V$. Its composite with the inclusion is the canonical $i$ of step 1: both functors send a local arrow triple to its specified isomorphism in $\mathcal X$, and stack descent glues these identifications. Consequently $[V/R]$ is DM and $i$ is a representable open immersion. Each scheme base change of $i$ is an open immersion, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale].
